definitions.explanation: Describes an action or state that continues without interruption. Somewhat more literary or formal than いつも.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}は{絶|た}えず{流|なが}れている。
{彼|かれ}は{絶|た}えず{新|あたら}しいことに{挑戦|ちょうせん}している。
examples.english: He is constantly challenging himself with new things.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}では{絶|た}えず{地震|じしん}の{危険|きけん}にさらされている。
examples.english: This region is constantly exposed to the danger of earthquakes.

notes:
USAGE:
{絶|た}えず is an adverb derived from the verb {絶|た}える (to cease, to run out) with the negative ず form. It literally means "without ceasing."

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {絶|た}えず: constantly, without interruption (slightly literary)
- いつも: always, at all times (everyday usage)
- {常|つね}に: invariably, at all times (formal)
- ずっと: continuously, the whole time (casual)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {絶|た}えず{変化|へんか}する (to change constantly)
- {絶|た}えず{努力|どりょく}する (to make constant effort)
- {絶|た}えず{流|なが}れる (to flow ceaselessly)
